title: Compact approximation from joint continuity on a compact column set
statement:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses, and suppose in addition that $Y$ is compact and that $f$ is jointly continuous on $X \times Y$. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a nonempty finite subset $u \subseteq X$ such that
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y) + \varepsilon;
\]
that is, restricting the row player to a suitable finite sample raises the lower value by at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: the convex-compact minimax hypotheses hold for $X$, $Y$, $f$ (both sets nonempty, $X$ compact and convex, $Y$ convex, $f$ continuous and convex in the row variable, concave in the column variable, and bounded above and below on $X\times Y$)
replaced:
Under the convex-compact minimax hypotheses, if $Y$ is compact and $f$ is jointly
continuous on $X \times Y$, then $\texttt{OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation}$
holds.  This is obtained by combining
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.theorem71\_uniformEquicontinuity\_of\_jointContinuous\_compact}$ with
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.theorem71\_compactApproximation\_of\_uniformEquicontinuity}$.
